title: 2016 AMC 10A Problem 6
statement: Ximena lists the whole numbers \(1\) through \(30\) once. Emilio copies Ximena’s numbers, replacing each occurrence of the digit \(2\) by the digit \(1.\) Ximena adds her numbers and Emilio adds his numbers. How much larger is Ximena’s sum than Emilio’s?

solutions.text:
When Emilio changes a units digit \(2\) to \(1\), his copied number is smaller by \(1\). This happens in \(2,12,22\), for a loss of \(3\).

When he changes a tens digit \(2\) to \(1\), his copied number is smaller by \(10\). This happens for \(20,21,\ldots,29\), for a loss of \(100\).

Thus Emilio’s sum is \(103\) less than Ximena’s sum, so Ximena’s sum is \(103\) larger.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Changing a units digit \(2\) to \(1\) loses \(1\)
Changing a tens digit \(2\) to \(1\) loses \(10\)
